failure_analysis.what_failed: On the sine scenarios the supervisor over-shifts the split toward high h1 / low h2. The pump-gain estimate uses the last sample only, k = f4/(0.8*v1), which is biased LOW whenever the voltage moves faster than tank4 can follow (PI overshoot or the 12 V limit): the measured h4-flow lags the pump voltage, so the code thinks pump 1 is weak. The predicted voltage for every candidate is then inflated, and the 2000 V^-1 saturation penalty dominates the 3000 m^-1 upper-level and band penalties, forcing splits that drive h2 below 0.25 m and h3 above 0.75 m (dev_feed_sine_2: 272 s band, 123 s upper, 1.11 m travel; dev_pump_sine_0 and dev_combined_sine_1 show the same over-shift signature).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: With the gain bias gone, re-examine the residual sine losses: the load residual (d1,d2) is still polluted by the tank level rates and by the supervisor's own transients, so a persistence/validity gate on the load estimate is the next candidate, not an averaging filter.

self_check: The pump-gain estimate is now the accumulation-corrected flow ratio (f4 + dh4/dt)/(0.8*v1) averaged over 30 s, which is an exact consequence of tank4's mass balance, so it is unbiased even while a pump saturates or the PI loop overshoots its new steady voltage. When a disturbance drives an upper level or a pump toward its limit, the candidate split is therefore scored with the true voltage requirement, and the supervisor shifts the split only as far as needed to keep h2 inside its band and h3/h4 below the limit instead of over-shifting and dragging h2 out of band. Production stays on target because every candidate keeps q1+q2 = Q exactly, so once the loops settle at any feasible split the reported Q equals the target.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample pump-gain estimate (f4/v1 with a min) by the accumulation-corrected ratio (f4 + dh4/dt)/(0.8*v1) averaged over the last 30 samples, for both pumps.
reason: beat the champion but candidate 2 scored lower

failure_analysis.what_failed: The oscillating-disturbance scenarios dominate the battery (feed mean 388.9, combined 222.2). The split is chosen from the instantaneous mass-balance load, but that estimate equals the true load minus the tank's own level rate, so it lags a swinging disturbance by tens of seconds; the supervisor's own 45 s post-move hold adds a second delay. The h1/h2 bias is therefore applied late in each cycle: the loops saturate (v1 = 12 V in the feed2 troughs) or push v2/h3 up (h3 = 0.85 m at the feed2 crests), so the actual levels leave the constant-Q curve (Q errors up to 1.7 L/s) while h2 drops out of its band and h3 exceeds its limit.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Tune only the two scalar parameters of the new lead (80 s horizon, 1.5 L/s clamp) if travel on step/ramp scenarios grows; do not additionally average or filter the load, since the flat-mean attempts (gen1 c1-c3, gen2 c2-c3) destroyed the sine response.

self_check: The split is now chosen for the load that is about to act, not the load that just acted: in a feed2 trough the predicted (more negative) load makes the optimizer move production to tank1 early, so pump 1 is not held at 12 V, h2 stays in its band and the actual pair stays on the constant-Q curve; towards a crest the predicted high load makes the h3 prediction exceed its target early, so h1 is held back and v2/h3 stay under their limits. The extrapolation is bounded to +/-1.5 L/s and the correction term (level rate) keeps the trend meaningful during the supervisor's own transients, so a step or ramp cannot trigger a runaway split; the existing travel penalty, 45 s hold and 0.06 m/call rate limit still cap setpoint motion. If the trend is wrong the error is at most about 0.05 m of h2 bias, which the soft constraint weights absorb.
proposed_change: Replace the instantaneous load used for the split decision with a lead-compensated load: the accumulation-corrected (level-rate-corrected) estimate is differenced over the last 60 s and extrapolated 80 s ahead, clamped to +/-1.5 L/s, so the setpoint bias leads a swinging disturbance instead of trailing it.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Oscillating disturbances dominate the battery (dev_feed_sine_2 1659, dev_feed_sine_1 872, dev_combined_sine_1 872, dev_pump_sine_0 535, dev_split_sine_1 402). During a sine the upper tanks fill and drain (large dh3/dt, dh4/dt), but the code derives the pump-flow estimate for the gain check from the steady-state relation Am=f4/0.8, Bm=f3/0.8. At t~1040 s of dev_feed_sine_2 this makes k1e read 0.00065 instead of 0.00085 (a fake 24% pump loss). The split optimizer then believes pump 1 is weak, so it shifts production onto pump 2 (h1 up, h2 down), which saturates v1 at 12 V, drives h3 above 0.75 m (123 s) and pushes h2 below its band (272 s), while Q sits 1-2 L/s off target.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If the corrected gains are not enough, next test a short 30-60 s mean of the accumulation-corrected pump flow, which removes the residual oscillation-driven gain bias without freezing the split response.

self_check: The split optimizer keeps its steady-state cost function, but the pump-flow inputs that set k1e and k2e now come from the upper-tank mass balance (outflow plus the measured level rate), so a transient fill or drain of tank3/tank4 is no longer mistaken for a 20-30% pump-gain loss. Because the model no longer believes a pump is weak, it stops shifting production onto the other pump, which keeps h3/h4 below the 0.75 m limit and keeps both voltages away from the 12 V rail instead of pinning one at saturation. The load term d1,d2 stays instantaneous, so the split still moves enough to keep h2 inside its band and Q on target during a real feed/pump/split disturbance, and the 0.06 m per call rate limit still caps the setpoint travel.
proposed_change: Compute the pump-flow estimates used for the gain estimates k1e and k2e from the upper-tank mass balance including the measured level rates, (f4+dh4/dt)/(1-gam1) and (f3+dh3/dt)/(1-gam2), while leaving the load estimate d1,d2 on the original static flows.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor chose setpoints by inverting the steady-state mass balances, implicitly assuming the PI loops sit exactly on their setpoints. When a feed/pump/split disturbance swings, the loops hold a proportional offset (e.g. h2 measured 0.44 m with setpoint 0.35 m, or 0.20 m with setpoint 0.30 m), so the levels actually achieved are setpoint+offset: produced Q swings by +-0.7-0.9 L/s (749 L off target on dev_feed_sine_2, 544 L on dev_feed_sine_1) and the achieved h2 leaves its band for 180-280 s, while the setpoint moves chosen by the split optimiser never aimed at the achieved level.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If this promotes, next look at the split-optimiser weights (3000 constraint vs 200 travel) and whether the upper-level prediction h3p/h4p should use measured accumulation, since combined_sine_0 still shows h3 above the limit.

self_check: Every candidate split is now scored on the levels and pump flows the plant will actually reach: the commanded setpoint is the desired achieved level minus the measured PI tracking offset (clamped to 0.12 m), so a swinging disturbance that leaves the loops lagging is compensated instead of being taken for the desired operating point. Because the achieved h2 is what enters the band cost, and the achieved production is pinned to the target by construction (q1+q2=target on achieved levels), both the production error and the h2 band excursions shrink. Pump saturation (predicted v1p or v2p above 12 V) and the upper-level limit are penalised in the same cost, so the split shifts production to the unloaded tank and keeps predicted h3/h4 below ulim-0.05; the offset clamp and the h2 setpoint clamp at h2_band+-0.05 keep the compensation from ever driving the setpoints wild.
proposed_change: Evaluate every candidate split on the levels the PI loops will actually achieve (setpoint plus the measured tracking offset off1=h1-sp_h1, off2=h2-sp_h2, clamped to +-0.12 m) and command setpoint = achieved_level - offset, instead of assuming the loops sit on their setpoints.

failure_analysis.what_failed: In the split optimizer the only voltage cost is the 2000-per-volt penalty above vmax=12 V, so whenever a disturbance pushes a pump the optimizer parks the demanded voltage right at the boundary (trace dev_feed_sine_2, t=460 s: chosen pair gives v1p=11.98 V while real v1=12.0 V is already saturated). With zero headroom the very next half-cycle of the feed oscillation saturates pump 1, the h2 loop loses authority, h2 dives to 0.204 m (below the 0.25 band) for 277 s and Q falls to 14.7 L/s, so both the band and the production objectives fail on the oscillating scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the voltage-margin mechanism and tune its size (margin and slope) on the oscillation scenarios; do not go back to filtering/averaging the load, which measurably loses on dev_feed_sine because it removes the in-phase correction that keeps h2 alive.

self_check: The split optimizer now prices predicted pump voltage above 11 V (12 V minus a 1 V margin) with a 700-per-volt slope on top of the existing hard 2000-per-volt penalty above 12 V, so it never parks a pump at the saturation boundary. When a disturbance would demand, say, 11.98 V from the tank2 chain, the extra cost makes the optimizer move production toward tank1 (h1 up, h2 down) until the predicted voltage is back inside the margin and the level the pump holds is achievable. That keeps the demanded h2 setpoint feasible, so h2 stays inside [0.25, 0.45], and it keeps 0.8*k1*v1 plus the tank4 drain able to supply the tank2 draw-off, so Q stays on target instead of collapsing when the pump saturates. The margin costs nothing at the nominal point (v1=9.0 V, v2=9.16 V), so steady operation and the production-target tracking are unchanged.
proposed_change: Add a soft 700-per-volt penalty on the predicted pump voltages above vmax-1.0 V in the setpoint-split cost, so the optimizer keeps a one-volt saturation margin instead of parking a pump at the 12 V limit.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The sine/oscillating scenarios dominate the battery (production off target is 77% of the score, band seconds 16%). In the two worst traces (dev_feed_sine_2, dev_feed_sine_1) a +/-2.5 L/s feed2 oscillation swings h2 by about +/-0.12 m with a ~360 s period. The supervisor's split bias is computed from the load estimate d1,d2 built on the upper-tank outflows f3,f4; during a swing the upper tanks store flow (dh4/dt + 0.25*dh3/dt appears in the residual), so the estimate lags the true load by the upper tank's storage time constant (~100 s). At each half-cycle the supervisor therefore keeps h2's setpoint high and h1 low (e.g. sp=[0.269,0.391] while the true draw-off is -2.46 L/s) exactly while the tank-2 loop is already saturated at v1=12 V; h2 then sits at 0.19-0.21 m, below the 0.25 band low, and Q runs about 1.5 L/s below target. The correct pair at that instant (h1~0.33, h2~0.31 with v1~12.0 V) is never commanded, so both the production integral and the band seconds grow; h3 also stays within 0.07 m of 0.75, so any extra tank-1 production must be headroom-limited.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the bounded measured-production feedback and, if it promotes, add the symmetric trim in the 'too little production' case via h2 restrained by the tank-4/v1 headroom; do not go back to level-derivative or low-pass load estimates, both measured worse than the lagged static estimate.

self_check: When the measured production is short the trim raises only the tank-1 setpoint, which raises pump 2, so the extra pump-2 flow (4/3 of the trim) is explicitly bounded by the tank-3 headroom: the guard compares the predicted pump-2 flow and the flow implied by the measured h3 against the flow that drives h3 to ulim-0.10, and simply refuses the upward trim when there is no room. The downward trim (production too high) is never blocked because it lowers pump 2 and h3, and it also pulls h2 down, which is what the band needs during the overshooting half-cycle. Both directions are hard-limited to 0.02 m of h1 and 0.4 L/s of flow, so the trim cannot dominate the model split, cannot drive a pump further into saturation (it lowers pump 1 by 1/3 of the trim when positive), and vanishes at steady state because the model pair is already on the constant-Q curve.
proposed_change: Add a bounded, measured-production-error feedback trim on the tank-1 setpoint (bounded by the tank-3/pump-2 headroom) so the split compensates the production error in phase with the actual error instead of relying only on the ~100 s-lagged load estimate.
